• Article 214 – Establishment of High Courts
• Article 215 – Court of Record

• Article 226 – Writ jurisdiction
• Article 227 – Superintendence
• Article 222 – Transfer of judges

items: Article 226 (Writ jurisdiction) is frequently compared with Article 32 (Supreme Court Writs) in constitutional law questions.
Article 215 establishes High Courts as a 'Court of Record', giving them the power to punish for contempt.
Article 222 governs the transfer of judges between different High Courts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 214 mandates the establishment of High Courts for states.
Article 215 declares the High Court to be a Court of Record.
Article 217 outlines the procedure for the appointment of High Court judges.
Article 222 provides for the transfer of judges from one High Court to another.
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of rights.
Article 227 gives High Courts power of superintendence over all subordinate courts.
